name: Boston Celtics
blurb: The winningest franchise in NBA history, built on a defense-first identity that dates back to Bill Russell's dynasty of the 1960s.

name: Brooklyn Nets
blurb: Born in the ABA as the New Jersey Americans, the franchise moved to Brooklyn in 2012 and rebuilt its identity around Barclays Center.

name: New York Knicks
blurb: One of the league's original franchises, playing every home game since inception at the world's most famous arena.

name: Philadelphia 76ers
blurb: Originally the Syracuse Nationals, the Sixers have produced some of the most dominant individual seasons in league history.

name: Toronto Raptors
blurb: The only franchise based outside the United States, and the first non-U.S. team to win an NBA championship, in 2019.

name: Chicago Bulls
blurb: Home to two three-peat championship runs in the 1990s, led by arguably the greatest player the game has produced.

name: Cleveland Cavaliers
blurb: Delivered the city of Cleveland its first major sports title in over 50 years with the 2016 championship comeback.

name: Detroit Pistons
blurb: The 'Bad Boys' era of the late 1980s defined physical, defense-first basketball and won back-to-back titles.

name: Indiana Pacers
blurb: An ABA powerhouse that carried its up-tempo identity into the NBA after the 1976 merger.

name: Milwaukee Bucks
blurb: Won a title in just its third season of existence, and returned to the top in 2021 behind a generational two-way star.

name: Atlanta Hawks
blurb: One of the league's oldest clubs, having relocated from the Tri-Cities to Milwaukee to St. Louis before settling in Atlanta.

name: Charlotte Hornets
blurb: Known for a passionate fan base and a teal-and-purple identity that remains one of the most recognizable in sports.

name: Miami Heat
blurb: Built a reputation on toughness and conditioning under coach Pat Riley, capturing three championships since 2006.

name: Orlando Magic
blurb: Reached two NBA Finals in its first decade behind two of the most dominant young centers in league history.

name: Washington Wizards
blurb: Won the franchise's only title as the Washington Bullets in 1978, behind a dominant frontcourt duo.

name: Denver Nuggets
blurb: A mile-high altitude advantage and a run-and-gun ABA pedigree, capped by the franchise's first title in 2023.

name: Minnesota Timberwolves
blurb: Anchored by one of the most versatile power forwards ever during the Kevin Garnett era of the late 1990s.

name: Oklahoma City Thunder
blurb: Formerly the Seattle SuperSonics, the franchise relocated in 2008 and built a young core around a trio of future MVPs.

name: Portland Trail Blazers
blurb: Won it all in its franchise-defining 1977 season and has fielded some of the most beloved rosters in the Pacific Northwest.

name: Utah Jazz
blurb: Defined by one of the greatest pick-and-roll partnerships ever between a point guard and power forward.

name: Golden State Warriors
blurb: Reinvented modern offense around three-point shooting during a dynasty that produced four titles in eight seasons.

name: LA Clippers
blurb: Long overshadowed by its crosstown rival, the franchise opened a new era with a purpose-built arena in Inglewood.

name: Los Angeles Lakers
blurb: Tied for the most championships in league history, spanning the Mikan, Magic, Shaq-Kobe, and LeBron eras.

name: Phoenix Suns
blurb: Pioneered the fast-paced 'Seven Seconds or Less' offense that reshaped how the modern game is played.

name: Sacramento Kings
blurb: The league's oldest continuously operating franchise, tracing its roots back to the Rochester Royals of 1945.

name: Dallas Mavericks
blurb: Captured its first title in 2011 behind one of the greatest playoff runs by a European-born superstar.

name: Houston Rockets
blurb: Back-to-back champions in the mid-1990s behind one of the most skilled centers ever to play the position.

name: Memphis Grizzlies
blurb: Built its identity on 'grit and grind' defense after relocating from Vancouver to Memphis in 2001.

name: New Orleans Pelicans
blurb: Renamed from the Hornets in 2013 to honor Louisiana's state bird, with a young core built around elite athleticism.

name: San Antonio Spurs
blurb: Five championships built on continuity, fundamentals, and one of the most successful coach-player pipelines ever.
